title: Cerf, Kahn, and the 1974 Paper That Defined TCP/IP
explainer: In 1974, Vint Cerf and Bob Kahn published 'A Protocol for Packet Network Intercommunication,' laying out the core ideas behind what became TCP/IP, the protocol suite that almost every network you configure as a developer still runs on. Their choice to push reliability logic into the endpoints rather than into the network itself is a key reason the internet could grow by linking independent networks instead of requiring one centrally managed one.

title: Paul Mockapetris and the Invention of DNS (1983)
explainer: Before 1983, computers on the early internet relied on a single, manually updated hosts file to map names to addresses, an approach that could not scale as the network grew. Paul Mockapetris designed the Domain Name System that year as a distributed, hierarchical replacement, and the basic design of resolvers, zones, and delegation is still what you depend on every time an application looks up a hostname today.
